content:
Mike H: Heads up — seeing out-of-order SSE events after reconnect in EU when session migrates between routing nodes. Repro on a multiplexed chat session: messages 1,2 sent, reconnect happens, then client receives 3 before 2.
Ana V: interesting — any console traces or per-route occupancy spikes?
Mike H: console shows a short blip on route eu-rt-12 then eu-rt-05 picks up. occupancy metric briefly doubles then corrects. Screenshot attached to thread (will ping separately).
Diana: is this the new least-loaded routing rollout that went out last night? I remember a change to prefer low-cpu nodes for session handoff.
Lee: yes, rollout rolled canary -> 50% around 02:13 UTC. change id: runtime/routing/2026-03-22/ld-prefer. Could be related.
Ana V: logs — here's a minimal sample from proxy:```
[2026-03-22T02:14:31Z] conn=abcd resume_id=xyz route=eu-rt-12 -> MIGRATE route=eu-rt-05
[2026-03-22T02:14:31Z] dispatch:event id=2 session=xyz node=eu-rt-12 status=ack
[2026-03-22T02:14:31Z] dispatch:event id=3 session=xyz node=eu-rt-05 status=sent
[2026-03-22T02:14:31Z] client_recv:event id=3 session=xyz
[2026-03-22T02:14:31Z] client_recv:event id=2 session=xyz
```
Mike H: note that node eu-rt-12 logged the ack for id=2 before migration, but client gets 3 first. feels like a short window where both nodes are allowed to emit events for the same session id.
Diana: Could be KV cache inconsistency — runtime allows a short dual-writer period during handoff. We have lease semantics but maybe the client resume is routed to new node before old node finishes flush.
Lee: routing config had a 200ms grace window added to reduce dropped events under load. That might be too long for multiplexed streams.
Selma (product): From UX side, the console is showing duplicated in-flight counts which confuses customers. We need a short-term mitigation for the dashboard while infra fixes root cause.
Ana V: propose three actions: 1) add a transient metric stream.session.dup_handoff increment when both nodes think they're primary, 2) tighten handoff grace to 20ms for canary group, 3) add console annotation so per-route counts show a "handoff in progress" hint.
Mike H: +1 for metric. I can add a debug flag in proxy to emit stream.handoff_debug for sessions where events out-of-order detected. minimal patch:```
--- a/proxy/streaming.go
+++ b/proxy/streaming.go
@@ -452,6 +452,10 @@ func handleHandoff(...) {
  // existing handoff
+  if detectOutOfOrder(session) {
+    metrics.Inc("stream.handoff_debug")
+  }
}
```
Lee: rolling a hotfix to canary cluster now with debug=on. DeployBot: canary deploy started: deploy/2026-03-22/handoff-debug -> eu-canary (id: d-9931).
DeployBot: canary deploy finished: 5 instances updated, health checks OK.
Diana: after canary, observed dup_handoff=37 in 10m window, mostly in multiplexed chat paths. confirms hypothesis.
Selma (product): For console UX, let's add a tooltip on per-route occupancy: "counts may be temporarily inflated during session handoffs" and show a small orange indicator when handoff metric spikes. Low-risk frontend change.
Ana V: agreement. I'll file the infra ticket to permanently fix handoff ordering — likely need strict single-writer semantics during resume, but that can increase tail latency under load. Tradeoff discussion needed.
Mike H: I captured a minimal reproducer script and will drop in the channel. For now, let's keep the tightened grace in rollout and the console annotation.
Lee: timeline: tighten grace to 20ms for canary -> monitor for 2h; if dup_handoff drops by >90% we widen rollout with metric gating.
Diana: also add quota note — if handoff causes duplicates then token accounting may double-bill for a short window. Ops: please verify billing side dedupe.
Ana V: pinging @billing-eng in a follow-up thread.
Selma (product): thanks team — I'll queue the frontend patch and coordinate messaging for the status page if customers notice spikes. :thumbsup:
Mike H: thanks everyone. I'll post follow-ups with logs and the reproducer.
